source.author: verg
source.text: Ne, pueri, ne tanta animis assuescite bella, neu patriae validas in viscera vertite vires; tuque prior, tu parce, genus qui ducis Olympo, proice tela manu, sanguis meus! Ille triumphata Capitolia ad alta Corintho victor aget currum, caesis insignis Achivis.
source.text_original: Ne, pueri, ne tanta animis assuescite bella, / neu patriae validas in viscera vertite vires; / tuque prior, tu parce, genus qui ducis Olympo, / proice tela manu, sanguis meus! — / 'Ille triumphata Capitolia ad alta Corintho / victor aget currum, caesis insignis Achivis.
source.text_english: Children, do not grow accustomed in your hearts to such great wars, nor turn the strong force of your country against its own vitals; and you, first of all, spare, you who lead your lineage from Olympus, cast away the weapons from your hand, my blood! He, victorious over Corinth, shall drive his chariot to the lofty Capitol in triumph, distinguished by slaughtered Achaeans.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Tum genitor vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_original: Tum genitor 'vetera haec nobis et condita pergunt / ordine cuncta suo rerumque a principe cursu / fixa manent; neque enim terris tum sanguis in ullis / noster erat, cum fata darem, iustique facultas / hinc mihi, cum varios struerem per saecula reges.
reuse.text_english: Then our father tells us these ancient things and all things, once established, continue in their own order and remain fixed in the course of events from the beginning of the world; for there was not yet any blood of ours on any lands when I was granting destinies, and from this came my power to rule justly, when I was setting up different kings through the ages.
